articles.title: Como v Manchester United: Champions League – live
articles.summary: ⚽️ Champions League updates from 5.45pm BST ⚽️ Live scoreboard | Champions League table | Mail Simon. Matthijs de Ligt comes in for Manchester United, making his first appearance since November last year, as Michael Carrick makes four changes.
body: Seven hundred Manchester United fans have made the trip to Lombardy, northern Italy, where Como 1907 play at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia (capacity 13,602), which is located on a shore of Lake Como. It is raining – hard – as kickoff approaches, as it has been since I arrived around 5.30pm local time on Tuesday. Como are billing this as the biggest game in their history, in what is their debut Champions League campaign. The big question for Michael Carrick’s team is simple: can they win only a third game of of the season here?

It’s a very special night, for the city, for the club. We’ve grown a lot and I think the players deserve to be living nights like this. Let’s enjoy it. A great honour for us. We have a very young team, we’re trying to create a culture, a style of play, which can take years. At the end of the day it’s conviction, to send a very clear idea, and a good thing about young players is they are not scared. Over the years, when you get older, is when you start maybe getting a little bit more worried.
Word is it’s going to be very seriously damp in Como this evening, and early photos from the ground suggest the afternoon hasn’t been much better.

articles.title: Andrews died of tear in artery around heart - autopsy
articles.summary: Former Sale player Hyron Andrews - who was found dead at his new team's hotel base before a Champions Cup match - died of natural causes, an autopsy finds.
body: Hyron Andrews - the former Sale second row found dead at his new team's hotel base before a Champions Cup match in France on Saturday - died of natural causes, an autopsy has found.
The 31-year-old, who joined the Johannesburg-based Lions this summer, suffered a tear in the aorta, an artery which carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.
The rupture led to blood filling the muscle sac surrounding his heart.

Andrews was found unconscious in a shower cubicle, with investigators working on the theory that he had either suffered a fall, a heart attack or, as transpired, an aneurysm, where a bulging blood vessel breaks.

articles.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
articles.summary: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well?
body: That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew?

Some people, like Holmes, think a documentary will help rebuild their reputation after public disgrace. When Anthony Weiner, who resigned from Congress after tweeting a photo of his bulging groin, tried to stage a professional comeback with a New York mayoral bid, he allowed cameras to film the journey. Only, he had more to hide: when further sex scandals emerged, his campaign went from a story of public redemption to innuendo-laden humiliation. And all the while, the cameras kept rolling. Weiner is a prime example of a subject losing control of the narrative.

Defensive lineman John ‌Franklin-Myers reportedly talked ‌Elliott down and no one was hurt. Elliott did ‌not practice Friday due to “personal reasons” and was inactive for Sunday’s 26-20 win against the Indianapolis Colts.
After reviewing the footage, the Titans opted to release the 28-year-old, who had signed a two-year, $8m ‌deal during the offseason.

Elliott appeared ​in the ​first five games of the season for the Titans. He has also played for the Cleveland Browns and San Francisco 49ers since the Browns picked him in the third round of the 2020 draft.

articles.title: Why do Man City fans boo pre-match anthems?
articles.summary: The cacophony of boos that greet the Premier League and Champions League anthems before kick-off have now become a fixture at Etihad Stadium.
body: The jeers from Manchester City fans were turned up a notch against Ipswich last Saturday when the side played their first home game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
"I can't remember a Premier League or Champions League home game where the anthems haven't been booed," City season-ticket holder Dave Wilson told BBC Sport.
The pre-match dissatisfaction towards top-flight chiefs can likely be traced back to February 2023, when the 115 charges for breaching the rules were first announced.
Later that same year, Everton had 10 points - reduced to six on appeal - deducted after being found to have broken profit and sustainability rules.

articles.title: Cancer campaigner Goodburn to deliver rugby match ball
articles.summary: Champion swimmer and brain cancer research campaigner Archie Goodburn will deliver the match ball for Scotland's Nations Championship match against Australia next month.
body: The Edinburgh-born 25-year-old has taken the campaign to bolster treatment and research to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney, in recent weeks.
And the Scottish 50m breaststroke record holder is delighted to be guest of honour at Murrayfield in his home city as the Wallabies visit on Sunday, 15 November.
"This means the absolute world to me," he said. "The most people I have ever performed in front of before was an audience of 10,000 on the castle esplanade for the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
"I was 12 and I sang a solo - What a Wonderful World! So this is an incredible opportunity to deliver the match ball in front of 60,000-plus people."

articles.summary: Barcelona report Paris Saint-Germain to Uefa after a tifo featuring a message which they say "incites violence and hatred in sport" was displayed ahead of Tuesday's Champions League match.

articles.title: Where Florida State's defense ranks in the ACC after Week 7
articles.summary: The Florida State Seminoles will be off this week before resuming their gauntlet of a schedule against the Clemson Tigers on Halloween, with a potentially ranked and definitely good Florida Gators team awaiting them at the end of it all.
body: Florida State football enters its bye week with a 3-4 record, most recently losing to No. 1 Miami, 43-35 in double overtime. Dropping its ACC record to 1-3, with Mike Norvell still looking for his first road win since 2023.

Through seven games, linebacker Chris Jones leads the team in tackles with 46 and is in fifth place in sacks. Defensive lineman Rylan Kennedy leads the team in sacks with six. Ashlyn Barker remains the team's leader in interceptions with two, with one coming in FSU's loss to Miami. The Seminoles have only logged four total interceptions this season, with the other two coming from Quindarrius Jones and Nehemiah Chandler, with one each.
As a team, how does FSU football's defense stack up against the rest of the ACC? Here is where the Seminoles rank in several major defensive categories through their first seven games.

Florida State is one of three teams in the conference that allow over 400 yards per game, at 434.9. Only the Stanford Cardinal is worse, at 452.0. Its best performance of the year came against Virginia, with the Seminoles only allowing 205 yards of offense.

articles.title: Michigan players praise QB Tommy Carr as film room junkie, vocal leader
articles.summary: Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr came in on Saturday and completely changed the energy of the entire team. After not scoring a single point in the first half, Michigan’s offense had multiple explosive runs and Carr took it in himself for what was ultimately the game-winning touchdown.
body: On Monday, head coach Kyle Whittingham elected not to share his plans at quarterback for the upcoming game with the reigning national champions coming to Ann Arbor. Reports, though, have since come out that Carr will start against No. 6 Indiana on Saturday.
Although Whittingham didn’t tip his hand on his secret plan, he did relay an intriguing sentiment about Carr’s work ethic.

“There’s not a quarterback that I’ve ever been around that studies more than Tommy Carr, and his football IQ is off the charts,” Whittingham said. “He’s got a great football mind. He’s a football junkie, and he is a real student of the game.”
Carr’s teammates echoed the same sentiments as their head coach on Tuesday when they talked in front of media members — notably mentioning Carr’s work ethic in the film room.

articles.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
articles.summary: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.
body: An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.
But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.
O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.

"We can't go into this game thinking about the points difference. We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga, and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough we're going to get the win."

articles.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
articles.summary: Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.
body: Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.
In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.
While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

articles.title: Conan, Doris, Crowley absent from Ireland's Nations Championship squad
articles.summary: Andy Farrell's Ireland will head into November's Nations Championship without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley, but Jamison Gibson-Park has been included.
body: Ireland face Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa next month without captain Caelan Doris and fly-half Jack Crowley, who are both expected to return from long-term injuries in January.

Doris has been sidelined by foot and knee problems, while Crowley is recovering from a vascular issue in his leg. Conan, who like Doris plays at No 8, is also ruled out after injuring his shoulder while playing for Leinster in the Champions Cup last weekend.

Scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park has yet to feature this season due to a groin injury but has been included in the 36-man squad. Mack Hansen, Andrew Porter and Ryan Baird also return to the squad after recovering from injury.
Two uncapped players have made the squad in Ulster fly-half Jamie Benson and back-row James McNabney, while Dan Sheehan has been named as captain.
